title: Locke and the social contract
examples: What is the difference between Hobbes and Locke's view on the state of nature?
Does the social contract mean we give up all our rights?
Who was the first philosopher to talk about the social contract?

explain.say: Today we look at big ideas about government. We will explore the concept of the social contract.

items: Concept: Gives structure to human life.
Example: Traffic laws keep us safe.

explain.say: Thomas Hobbes thought life without government would be a war. He called this state of nature a war of all against all.

draw.text: Hobbes: War of all against all

explain.say: John Locke believed people have natural rights even without government. These rights include life, liberty, and property.
Jean-Jacques Rousseau suggested people are naturally good. Society and private property can corrupt these natural goodnesses.
So, why do we have governments? We form governments to protect our natural rights. We agree to certain limits on our freedom for safety.
Think about playing a sport like football. You must follow rules to play fairly. This is like a real-life social contract.

faq.q: What exactly is the state of nature?
faq.a: It is a hypothetical time before any government or laws existed. Think of it as life without rules.
asks: What did life feel like before governments?
Can you describe a life without laws?

faq.q: Do all philosophers agree on the social contract?
faq.a: No, they disagree strongly. Hobbes saw it as necessary for survival, while Locke focused on protecting existing rights.
asks: Are all views on contracts the same?
Who disagreed the most about government?

faq.q: If the government breaks the contract, what happens?
faq.a: Locke suggested the people have the right to challenge or overthrow a government that fails its duty.
asks: Can people rebel against bad governments?
What is the people's right if the government fails?

faq.a: Philosophically, they are seen as inherent rights given by nature or God, not by rulers. They exist regardless of laws.
asks: Do we get rights from the government?
Are rights something given to us?

faq.q: What does 'liberty' mean in this context?
faq.a: Liberty means the freedom to act and speak without undue restraint from others or the state.
asks: Is liberty the same as freedom?
What is the difference between freedom and license?

facts: Hobbes believed life without government would be 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'.
Locke argued that the primary purpose of government is to protect property and life.
Rousseau emphasized that society can corrupt the natural goodness of man.
The concept suggests that individuals consent to be governed.

quiz.say: If a society establishes rules to keep peace, what concept is it enacting?

options.show: Agreement among people to form a governing body.
options.say: Agreement among people to form a governing body.

options.show: A natural law that always exists.
options.say: A natural law that always exists.

options.show: A physical force keeping things together.
options.say: A physical force keeping things together.

quiz.why: This describes the mutual consent that forms the basis of organized society.

wrong.0: The contract is an agreement, not just a piece of paper.
wrong.2: This confuses the social contract with inherent moral rules.
wrong.3: This confuses a social concept with a scientific force.

quiz.say: According to Locke, what is the most important right government must protect?

options.show: The right to own land only.
options.say: The right to own land only.

options.show: The protection of life, liberty, and property.
options.say: The protection of life, liberty, and property.

quiz.why: Locke specifically identified these three rights as fundamental to human existence.

wrong.0: This is too narrow; Locke included liberty and life as well.
wrong.2: This focuses only on political participation, ignoring personal safety.
wrong.3: While important, Locke stressed limited rights for stability.

quiz.say: If a government becomes tyrannical and abuses its power, what might a philosopher like Locke suggest?

options.show: The people may have the right to resist or change the government.
options.say: The people may have the right to resist or change the government.

options.show: They must obey no matter what.
options.say: They must obey no matter what.

options.show: They must wait for a revolution.
options.say: They must wait for a revolution.

options.show: They can only complain to a higher power.
options.say: They can only complain to a higher power.

quiz.why: This reflects Locke's idea that government power comes from the consent of the governed.

wrong.1: This ignores the conditional nature of the social contract.
wrong.2: Locke suggested a right to action, not just waiting for a specific event.
wrong.3: This limits the people's practical recourse within the political system.
